items.title: HAI Digital Economy Lab dashboards track AI's footprint on the labor market
items.summary_en: HAI describes dashboards from its Digital Economy Lab that track how AI adoption relates to employment and wider economic indicators, including a Transformation Tracker, a Canaries Dashboard built with ADP Research, an Adoption Monitor and a GDP-B Surplus Observer. Reported early findings include a decline of over 3% a year in employment among 22- to 25-year-olds in software development and customer service since late 2022.
items.notes: Date from HAI listing via snippet. Dashboards reportedly launched June 2026. Researchers caution ADP data may not be fully representative. Full text not read.

items.title: Shah and Chen: Measuring what medical AI can actually do
items.summary_en: Nigam Shah and Jonathan Chen write about three years spent building harder, more realistic benchmarks for medical AI. The teaser also says new Stanford research finds that benchmarks for safety, bias and reasoning often fail to measure what they claim to.

items.title: Q&A: Who is responsible when AI causes harm?
items.summary_en: A Shana Lynch piece features Deb Raji on accountability when AI systems cause harm. Raji argues that obscuring the link between actions and outcomes is how accountability disappears. She joins HAI as a Visiting Fellow this fall.
